test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Consider that a mature blue whale is 30.0 m long. On the other hand a baby whale is 10.0 m long. Where should the baby whale be placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15.0 m so that one can observe a real image of the baby whale as that of the size of a mature whale?
solution:
The correct answer is 2__**0 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

**Step 1: Calculate the Required Magnification**

Given

__
 
• Length of mature whale h_i= -30m
 
• Length of baby whale h_o= 10m

The magnification required is: m= (h_i)/(h_o)= (-30)/(10)=-3

This means the image needs to be three times the size of the object.

**Step 2: Apply Magnification Formula for Mirrors**

The magnification (m) is also related to the object distance (p) and the image distance (q) by: m=-(q)/(p)

We know m = -3, So (q)/(p)= -3

q=-3p

**Step 3: Use the Mirror Formula**

The mirror formula is: (1)/(f)= (1)/(p)+(1)/(q), where f is the focal length of the mirror.

Given the focal length of the mirror f=-15m, substitute q=-3p into the mirror formula:

(1)/(-15)=(1)/(-p)+ (1)/(-3p)

-(1)/(15)=( -3-1)/(3p)

(1)/(15)=(4)/(3p)

p=20

 

The baby whale should be placed **20.0 m in front of the concave mirror** to produce a **real image three times the size of the baby whale**, making it appear as long as a mature whale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with its reflecting surface curved inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It can form real and virtual images depending on the position of the object relative to the focal point and center of curvature.
 
• When an object is placed beyond the center of curvature, the image formed is real, inverted, and diminished.
 
• When an object is placed between the focal point and the center of curvature, the image formed is real, inverted, and magnified.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• The focal length of a mirror is the distance between the mirror's surface and its focal point, where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting off the mirror.
 
• For a concave mirror, the focal length is positive, indicating that the focal point is on the same side as the reflecting surface.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• The mirror formula relates the object distance (u), the image distance (v), and the focal length (f) of a spherical mirror:
 
• (1)/(f)=(1)/(v)+(1)/(u)
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m):**
 
 
• Magnification is the ratio of the height of the image (h') to the height of the object (h), which can also be expressed in terms of distances:
 
• m=(h')/(h)=-(v)/(u)
